# Jonah

::: {.book-summary}
## Book Summary Insight

Jonah reveals God's compassion for all nations through the reluctant prophet's mission to Nineveh. The book teaches that God's mercy extends far beyond Israel.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 1

<div class="key-verse">Jonah 1:17</div>

<div class="identifier">The LORD prepared a great fish</div>

### Why This Verse

Most recognized event in Jonah

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Jonah's attempt to flee from God's call. The key verse demonstrates that no one can escape God's presence or purposes.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 2

<div class="key-verse">Jonah 2:9</div>

<div class="identifier">Salvation is of the LORD</div>

### Why This Verse

Central theological statement

### Chapter Insight

This chapter contains Jonah's prayer from inside the great fish. The key verse emphasizes that salvation and deliverance belong to the Lord alone.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 3

<div class="key-verse">Jonah 3:10</div>

<div class="identifier">God repented of the disaster</div>

### Why This Verse

Nineveh's repentance

### Chapter Insight

This chapter recounts Jonah's preaching in Nineveh and the city's repentance. The key verse highlights God's mercy toward those who genuinely turn from sin.
:::

::: {.chapter-entry}
## Chapter 4

<div class="key-verse">Jonah 4:2</div>

<div class="identifier">Gracious and merciful, slow to anger</div>

### Why This Verse

Jonah's complaint and God's character

### Chapter Insight

This chapter records Jonah's anger over God's compassion toward Nineveh. The key verse reveals God's concern for all people and His desire to show mercy.
:::
